A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same procedural warm-up method for vision transformers. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the additional Appendix C in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification and transfer experiments, training curves, and ablations in Section 4, Tables 2–8, and Figures 2–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds a baseline variant, vocabulary-size results, and results with seed variability in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The formal-language generators, frozen token and positional embeddings, masked-token objective, and transition to image training remain unchanged. The added vocabulary sweep evaluates a parameter of the existing method; retaining FractalDB embeddings changes a comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six image-classification datasets, FractalDB, and WW, k-DYCK, and k-DYCK SHUFFLE generators. Appendix C reuses existing datasets and tasks without introducing a new domain or test scenario.

E2.justification: New Table 10 adds FractalDB warm-up with retained pretrained patch embeddings as a comparator on five datasets. The default, Mimetic, and embedding-reset FractalDB comparisons in Tables 2 and 3 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds an embedding-retention control for FractalDB and a k=16, 32, 64, 80 vocabulary-parameter sweep. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; the explicit fine-tuning batch size of 512 clarifies documentation rather than establishing a changed setting.

E4.justification: Tables 10 and 11 add focused analyses of whether resetting FractalDB embeddings disadvantages that baseline and how vocabulary size affects procedural warm-up. The existing grammar, token-order, warm-up-duration, weight-shuffling, and layer-transfer analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Unlike v1's point estimates, Table 12 reports mean ± standard deviation over three random seeds for four methods on Tiny-ImageNet and CIFAR-100. This newly documents replication and uncertainty for a limited subset; it does not establish that the run count increased.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation results remain unchanged. Table 10 adds embedding-retaining FractalDB results, including 67.35% on CIFAR-100 versus 64.61% with embeddings reset. Table 11 reports 69.05%, 69.78%, 71.98%, and 71.83% for k=16, 32, 64, and 80. These are additional setting-specific results, not revised performance under the original settings.

T1.justification: The formal-language descriptions, hierarchy classifications, ambiguous-completion discussion, and mathematical reasoning are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims of beneficial nonvisual warm-up, complementarity with image pretraining, and benefits concentrated in later layers. The headline ImageNet improvement and claim that 1% procedural training can replace 28% of image examples are unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 corrects the contradictory statement that simple repetition does lead to useful mechanisms to does not, aligning it with the unchanged WW results. Section 5 removes speculation that tasks beyond classification might obtain even larger benefits, while retaining the main applicability limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project/code link, explicitly specifies batch size 512 for downstream fine-tuning, and explains that equal input sizes make example and token budgets proportional. The existing optimizer, learning rates, training durations, and generator details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The contribution statement explicitly foregrounds the extension of prior procedural LLM pretraining to ViTs, and reference [60] changes its cited structured-initialization preprint from 2404.01139 to 2505.19985. The broader positioning is retained. The anonymous procedural-pretraining reference in v1 matches the named Jiang et al. entry in v2 and is not a new work.

P1.justification: v2 tightens the abstract, related work, Section 4.2, and limitations; corrects wording and appendix cross-references; and adds Appendix C. The main section sequence and explanatory narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds appendix Tables 10–12, compacts Table 9, and resizes or repositions Figures 3 and 4. Several captions and surrounding layouts are tightened, while the original plots and main table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: Appendix C strengthens the evidence by testing FractalDB with retained embeddings, examining vocabulary sensitivity, and exposing seed variability on two datasets. These additions address specific comparison and reliability questions without changing the main results. Clearer training documentation and corrected interpretation further improve the paper, but the gains remain focused rather than a substantial scientific revision.
